item.title: Reports: Argentina coach Scaloni set to renew contract
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni looks on ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup Group J soccer match between Argentina and Algeria at Kansas City Stadium. (is associated with: «Reports: Argentina coach Scaloni set to renew contract») Tom Weller/dpa Coach Lionel Scolani is reportedly set for a contract extension to lead Argentina into the post-Lionel Messi era. La Nación paper said that "only the signature is missing" while Clarín said a little more cautiously that Scolani and Argentina FA president Claudio Tapia have made progress in both parties' aim for a renewal until the 2030 World Cup. The reports said that Scaloni could receive a contract until the Copa America in 2028 with an option to renew it until 2030 World Cup which includes one match in Argentina. Scolani, 48, was appointed in 2018 and led the team captained by Messi to the 2022 World Cup title and the 2026 final, plus Copa America success in 2021 and 2024. Messi has now retired from the national team while Scolani had at first left it open whether he would renew his contract which expires at the end of the year.

item.title: Rennes predicted XI v Juventus: Esteban Lepaul out, Franck Haise to move to back three
item.description: Rennes predicted XI v Juventus: Esteban Lepaul out, Franck Haise to move to back three Esteban Lepaul withdrew late on in Stade Rennais’ 4-3 loss to Paris FC with an ankle injury. The France international has not recovered in time to face Juventus in the UEFA Europa League later tonight. In his absence, Franck Haise is set to start with two strikers. Boulaye Dia is set to partner Moussa Al-Taamari. With Lepaul out, Rennes’ whole shape is expected to change. The Breton club are expected to start with a back three, with former England youth international Charlie Cresswell starting at the heart of it. Mahamadou Nagida is set to once again start over Quentin Merlin, who has seemingly dropped down the pecking order. Bryan Reynolds, meanwhile, is set to continue at right-back in Turin tonight. Valentin Rongier will captain the French side. Rennes likely line-up v Juventus Brice Samba; Mahamadou Nagida, Anthony Rouault, Charlie Cresswell, Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal, Bryan Reynolds; Mahdi Camara, Valentin Rongier, Sébastien Szymanski; Boulaye Dia, Moussa Al-Taamari. (L’Éq) GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Rockets’ Kevin Durant hilariously drops mic on Jabari Smith Jr.’s big night
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Rockets’ Kevin Durant hilariously drops mic on Jabari Smith Jr.’s big night appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Rockets leaned on the prolific scoring of Kevin Durant and Jabari Smith Jr. to dispose of the Dallas Mavericks, 128-110, in their season opener at Toyota Center on Wednesday. Durant had 30 points on 10-of-16 shooting, six rebounds, and three assists, while Smith added 30 points on 11-of-17 shooting, including 4-of-8 from long range, five rebounds, and two steals. Smith was four points shy of tying his career-high. He was efficient with his shot selection. In the postgame conference, Durant was asked about Smith’s decision-making, and the two-time Finals MVP gave a witty answer . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “His decision to go get 30. That was the most important thing,” said Durant in the video posted by Locked On Network’s Jackson Gatlin, eliciting laughter in the media room. Asked Kevin Durant what he saw with Jabari Smith Jr.'s decision-making tonight: "His decision to go get 30." pic.twitter.com/vx4wsDU90w — Jackson Gatlin (@JTGatlin) October 22, 2026 No burner account needed for that hilarious burn. Fans on X showed love to the 23-year-old Smith for his impressive showing. “Jabari’s been hooping like he got something to prove lately,” said @sofx83. “Talk about efficient 🔥🎯 #allfire,” added @Htown_Aggie. “KD and Bari 30-piece? We’re going far this year,” declared @teekev8. “I hope this is his year, man,” commented @TProfty. “Gonna go down as the best player in 2022 class,” claimed @rocketsdon. With his length and versatility, Smith has a high upside. He, however, has yet to fully learn how to maximize them. He has shown steady improvement, and the guidance of Durant should help him become a well-rounded player. Last season, Smith averaged a career-high 15.8 points on 45% shooting and 6.9 rebounds in 77 games. The Rockets will take on the San Antonio Spurs on Friday. Related: Rockets’ Tari Eason earns first ejection of new NBA season for shoving PJ Washington Related: Watch Kevin Durant posterize Cooper Flagg on emphatic slam dunk

item.title: Warriors face major Kristaps Porzingis setback as Stephen Curry speaks out
item.description: Photo by Tayfun Coskun/Anadolu via Getty Images Stephen Curry has admitted the Golden State Warriors face a difficult situation after Kristaps Porzingis was reportedly sidelined indefinitely with a health issue that has left him considering retirement. The Latvian centre was expected to play a key role for Golden State this season after signing a two-year, $40 million contract extension during the offseason. However, recurring symptoms of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) have disrupted those plans, leaving the Warriors uncertain about when, or whether, he will return. Stephen Curry admits Kristaps Porzingis uncertainty is difficult for Golden State Warriors Speaking after Golden State’s 127-105 defeat to the Los Angeles Lakers, Curry acknowledged the impact Porzingis’ situation has had on both the player and the team. “It’s a hard one for all reasons,” Curry said, as reported by ESPN’s Anthony Slater. “Personally, first and foremost. Then us as a team…We always said availability was a big factor for our team. It’s no secret that (center) spot was an important one for us, especially with the skillset.” The four-time NBA champion also stressed the importance of considering Porzingis’ wellbeing rather than focusing solely on basketball. “It’s hard to talk about it without keeping the humanity in mind,” Curry said. He added that the Warriors had seen what their roster could achieve with Porzingis involved but now needed to find a way forward. “We have to overcome that obviously, but we’d love to have him here,” Curry said. Curry also revealed he had not spoken to Porzingis since the start of training camp, underlining the uncertainty surrounding the situation. Golden State confirmed that discussions involving Porzingis, the franchise and his representatives would remain private. The organisation also said it was not expecting the centre to be around the team in the immediate future. Porzingis reportedly met with Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy and medical chief Rick Celebrini to discuss his future, with retirement among the possibilities being considered. The Warriors are also reportedly exploring potential trade options, although a buyout or an application for a league exception have also been discussed. For now, Golden State must prepare without a player who was expected to strengthen its centre position. Further updates will depend on Porzingis’ health and the outcome of discussions with the franchise. Read more: Stephen A. Smith says he already knows when LeBron James is going to retire ‘He was talking trash’: Anthony Edwards says Miami Heat player got him all fired up ‘His mindset needs to change’: Shaquille O’Neal ‘baffled’ by LaMelo Ball’s Timberwolves comment

item.title: Carrick in danger? Nagelsmann emerges as potential replacement
item.description: Carrick in danger? Nagelsmann emerges as potential replacement Michael Carrick is under enormous pressure as Manchester United manager after Wednesday’s 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League extended the Red Devils’ winless run to seven matches. According to talkSPORT, Manchester United appear to be preparing for life without Carrick and have identified Julian Nagelsmann —the former Bayern Munich and Germany manager—as their leading candidate to replace him. The 39-year-old, who stepped down as Germany manager after a disappointing World Cup, was linked with the job before Carrick was appointed permanently in May and reportedly has supporters among the club’s senior leadership. Another German coach, Fabian Hürzeler—currently in charge of Brighton & Hove Albion—is also a candidate, alongside Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe. item.title: Magic star Paolo Banchero speaks up on tense confrontation with Jalen Johnson
item.description: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Magic star Paolo Banchero speaks up on tense confrontation with Jalen Johnson appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Paolo Banchero says he was not the one who started his heated exchange with Jalen Johnson at the end of the Orlando Magic ’s season opener. He just was not about to walk away from it. The Magic forward and the Atlanta Hawks star had to be separated by teammates and staffers as the final buzzer sounded on Atlanta’s 132-125 win on Wednesday night at Kia Center. After the game, Banchero was asked about the incident by Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel, and he made it clear who he felt started it. “Yeah, he wanted to wait ‘til the clock hit zero to say something to me,” Banchero said. “So, I just wanted to hear what he said. But it is what it is. Game one.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) I asked #Magic forward Paolo Banchero about this postgame interaction with Jalen Johnson : “Yeah, he wanted to wait ‘til the clock hit zero to say something to me,” Banchero said. “So, I just wanted to hear what he said. But it is what it is. Game one.” Video: https://t.co/oRb1DjVdld pic.twitter.com/x80taEcqdI — Jason Beede (@therealBeede) October 22, 2026 Banchero did not reveal what Johnson said, and the exact trigger for the confrontation remains unclear. Larry Brown Sports pointed to a battle for a rebound in the closing moments as a possible spark. Either way, Banchero sounded ready to move on. His “game one” remark served as a reminder that there is a long season ahead, with plenty more meetings to come between the two Southeast Division rivals. Both players are former Duke standouts, which adds another layer to the matchup. The frustration was understandable given how the night played out . Banchero was spectacular, finishing with 35 points on 10-of-12 shooting, seven rebounds and 10 assists. Johnson countered with 20 points and 14 rebounds for Atlanta. Orlando battled back from a 10-point halftime deficit and took a 100-99 lead into the fourth quarter. But a key replay review went Atlanta’s way with 4:27 left, when an offensive foul that would have been Johnson’s sixth was overturned after the Hawks challenged it. Nickeil Alexander-Walker then took over down the stretch, hitting two three-pointers in the final two minutes on his way to 31 points. Dyson Daniels added 20 points and five steals, while CJ McCollum chipped in 19. Wendell Carter Jr. and Franz Wagner each scored 22 for the Magic, and Desmond Bane added 18. The loss spoiled the debut of first-year head coach Sean Sweeney and extended Atlanta’s winning streak in the series to six games. Banchero and the Magic will look to bounce back when they host the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday. Related: Desmond Bane pinpoints where Magic got ‘killed’ by Hawks Related: NBA stars Paolo Banchero, Jalen Johnson have to be seperated after tense end to Hawks-Magic

item.title: Liverpool in driving seat for fourth £100m deal this winter
item.description: Liverpool in driving seat for fourth £100m deal this winter Liverpool have been a free-spending club for the last three windows, adding over £650 million worth of talent. Andoni Iraola didn’t walk into a squad ready to compete however, and there is still plenty of work to be done in the transfer market as well as on the training ground before the Reds can compete on all fronts again. Several areas need addressing over the next 9 months, but one of the most pressing is Liverpool’s midfield. Too often under Iraola the Reds have lost the midfield battle, and their weakness has affected results. It is clear that Liverpool need to add a midfielder, and a recent report suggests that they are in the driving seat for one who could cost £100 million. Liverpool in pole position for another £100 million player Earlier this season Liverpool became the first team to field three players that cost over £100 million at the same time. By the end of January they could become the first team to field four. Bournemouth’s Alex Scott has been the subject of many discussions among the Anfield faithful in recent weeks, the Bournemouth man is reportedly held in high regard by Iraola and he could well be heading to Merseyside this winter. That’s according to a report from Mail Sport , which claims that sources at Bournemouth believe that Liverpool are not only serious in the chase for Scott, but are actually in the driving seat due to Iraola’s connection with the 23-year-old. As it is expected that Scott will demand a fee of over £100 million, many Reds will be surprised to hear that Iraola’s side lead Chelsea in the battle for the England international. Liverpool have proven that they are not afraid to spend in recent windows though, and there is little evidence to suggest that their spending spree is done yet. The report does point out that it would be in Bournemouth’s interest to make Chelsea believe that Liverpool are winning the race to try and encourage a bold bid in the winter. There is no doubt that the Reds’ interest is genuine, but their capacity or willingness to spend another £100 million mid-season is a doubt. With only 18 months remaining on his contract it feels like Scott’s future will be decided sooner rather than later, but it isn’t yet clear what that means for Liverpool.

item.title: Ranji Trophy: Mohit Avasthi takes five as Mumbai thrash Himachal Pradesh by an innings and 97 runs
item.description: Seamer Mohit Avasthi returned five for 44 in 16 overs, the seventh five-wicket haul of his firstclass career, to bowl Mumbai to an innings-and-97-run victory over Himachal Pradesh on the final day of their Elite Group D Ranji Trophy match at the Luhnu Cricket Ground in Bilaspur on Wednesday. The emphatic victory earned Mumbai a bonus point for the second match in a row, taking them to the top of the table with 14 points from two matches. Resuming on 144 for three, Himachal put up a gallant fight, batting for 99.1 overs and stretching their second-innings total to 291, after having folded inside 40 overs in the first innings. Wicketkeeper-batter Vaibhav Kalta (63, 169b, 10x4) and captain Pukhraj Mann (50, 126b, 6x4) delayed Mumbai’s charge by adding 85 in 197 balls for the fourth wicket. The resistance ended when Mann was caught by Musheer Khan off Tushar Deshpande. Avasthi struck soon after lunch, having Arpit Guleria (6) caught by Musheer, before Mumbai completed the formalities. Apart from Avasthi, Deshpande took two for 60 to finish with match figures of six for 106, while the tireless Shams Mulani claimed two for 52. After losing to Bengal in their opening match, Delhi picked up three points to open their account, while Gujarat had to settle for one. In reply to Delhi’s 648 for six declared, Gujarat made 479. The resistance ended when Mann was caught by Musheer Khan off Tushar Deshpande. Avasthi struck soon after lunch, having Arpit Guleria (6) caught by Musheer, before Mumbai completed the formalities. Apart from Avasthi, Deshpande took two for 60 to finish with match figures of six for 106, while the tireless Shams Mulani claimed two for 52. RANJI ROUNDUP Group A: In Puducherry: Pondicherry 177 & 98/1 drew with Madhya Pradesh 345; Group B: In New Chandigarh: Punjab 456 & 86/3 bt Chhattisgarh 206 & (f/o) 335 (Aayush Pandey 111, Amandeep Khare 62; Harjas Singh 3/92, Emanjot Singh Chahal 3/43) by 7 wickets; In Mulapadu: Hyderabad 275 & 306/7d bt Andhra 184 & 130 (Tanay Thyagarajan 6/35) by 267 runs; In Alur: Karnataka 342 & 243/7d (KV Aneesh 79; Parth Bhut 3/80) drew with Saurashtra 349 & 137/2 (Chirag Jani 63*); Group C: In Thiruvananthapuram: Kerala 404 beat Odisha 225 & 143 (Jalaj Saxena 5/34) by an inns & 36 runs; In New Delhi: Delhi 648/6d drew with Gujarat 479 (Manan Hingrajia 123, Chintan Gaja 82; Hrithik Shokeen 5/143) & 15/1; In Pune: Jharkhand 169 & 344/8 (Shikhar Mohan 127) drew with Maharashtra 527/5d; Group D: In Bilaspur: Himachal Pradesh 140 & 291 (Pukhraj Mann 50, Vaibhav Kalta 63; Mohit Avasthi 5/44) lost to Mumbai 528/8d by an inns & 97 runs; In Jaipur: Rajasthan 497 drew with Railways 338 (Eshaan Goyal 64, Bhargav Merai 73, Ravi Singh 53, Toufik Mondal 53*) & 174/2 (Mohammad Saif 103*; Chetan Sharma 1/8) Delhi-Gujarat tie ends in a high-scoring draw The Delhi-Gujarat match at the Palam ground in New Delhi ended in a high-scoring draw, with the players shaking hands at tea. After losing to Bengal in their opening match, Delhi picked up three points to open their account, while Gujarat had to settle for one. In reply to Delhi’s 648 for six declared, Gujarat made 479. Punjab’s Gill misses out on batting in second innings After being dismissed for one in the first innings against Chhattisgarh at Mullanpur in New Chandigarh, India’s Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill missed out on batting in the second innings after being off the field for the entire day on Wednesday. Prabhsimran Singh (24) batted at Gill’s usual No. 4 position. Following up his 161 in the first innings, the Punjab captain then smashed an unbeaten 40 off just 36 balls to steer his side to a seven-wicket victory. Punjab chased down their 86-run target by the 17th over on the final day.

item.title: Highest successful run chases in all T20 cricket at Hagley Oval, Christchurch: Full list of records including T20Is
item.description: Highest successful run chases in all T20 cricket at Hagley Oval, Christchurch: Full list of records including T20Is originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Pakistan's 177/3 against Bangladesh in 2022 is the highest successful T20I chase at Hagley Oval. Only eight teams have chased down a target in a T20I at the ground. Canterbury's 222/3 in the 2019-20 Super Smash is the highest successful chase in all T20 cricket there. Highest successful run chases in T20Is at Hagley Oval Hagley Oval has never been a ground where enormous totals get run down, which matters a great deal with India set to chase in the opening T20I of their series against New Zealand. The highest successful pursuit in a men's T20I here remains Pakistan's 177/3 against Bangladesh, and that was four years ago. Pakistan reached it with a ball to spare on October 13, 2022, during the tri-series that New Zealand hosted ahead of the T20 World Cup. That tournament accounts for a remarkable share of the ground's chasing history, with five of the eight successful chases coming inside a fortnight in October of that year. Only eight teams have chased down a target at the venue in T20I cricket, and the margins tell their own story. Three of those pursuits went into the 19th over or beyond, and New Zealand's 92/1 against Pakistan in March 2025 is on the list only because the visitors had been dismissed for 91. Team Score Overs Opposition Date Pakistan 177/3 19.5 v Bangladesh 13 Oct 2022 Pakistan 168/5 19.3 v New Zealand 14 Oct 2022 New Zealand 159/3 18.1 v Pakistan 19 Jan 2024 England 154/3 18.3 v New Zealand 1 Nov 2019 Pakistan 149/4 18.2 v New Zealand 8 Oct 2022 New Zealand 142/2 17.5 v Bangladesh 9 Oct 2022 New Zealand 131/1 16.1 v Pakistan 11 Oct 2022 New Zealand 92/1 10.1 v Pakistan 16 Mar 2025 MORE: Samson vs Santner in all T20 cricket Highest successful run chases in domestic T20 cricket at Hagley Oval The domestic game has produced the one genuinely big chase the ground has seen. Canterbury scored 222/3 in 18.5 overs against Northern Districts in the 2019-20 Super Smash. They won that match by seven wickets with seven balls to spare, and it stands as the only successful chase beyond 200 in any T20 at the venue. As Canterbury's home ground, the venue has hosted the Super Smash final on several occasions, with the last two both settled by the team batting second. Northern Brave chased 155 in the 2022-23 decider, reaching 156/3 in 18 overs, and returned in January 2026 to overhaul Canterbury's 171/5 with 13 balls remaining. Across all T20 cricket at the ground, chasing sides have generally held the advantage. The venue has seen first-innings totals average around 150 in Super Smash cricket, and the second innings has historically been the easier time to bat under lights. item.title: Nickeil Alexander-Walker pours in 31, leads Hawks to season-opening 132-125 win over Magic
item.description: Atlanta Hawks guard Nickeil Alexander-Walker, right, pushes against Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. during the first half of an NBA basketball game, Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026, in Orlando, Fla. (AP Photo/John Raoux) John Raoux Nickeil Alexander-Walker punctuated a 31-point night with a pair of 3-pointers, Dyson Daniels and Jalen Johnson each finished with 20 points, and the Atlanta Hawks beat the Orlando Magic 132-125 in the season opener for both teams on Wednesday night. Paolo Banchero had 35 points and 10 assists for the Magic, who have lost six straight the Hawks. Atlanta also spoiled coach Sean Sweeney’s debut with Orlando. Alexander-Walker hit a 3 before flashing a hush gesture to the Kia Center crowd and then drained a 25-footer that gave Atlanta a 128-123 lead with 51 seconds left. Franz Wagner and Wendell Carter Jr. each had 22 points for Orlando. TRENDING STORIES: Atlanta Dream dominate Game 3 of WNBA finals Johnson appeared to foul out with 4:27 remaining when officials called him for an offensive foul after an elbow to the face of Desmond Bane. However, Atlanta coach Quin Snyder successfully challenged the call with replay showing Bane committing the first illegal contact. Leading 120-117 at the time, the Hawks never trailed over the balance of the game. C.J. McCollum scored 19 points and Aaron Wiggins added 16 for Atlanta. Banchero sparked an 11-0 run and gave the Magic their first lead of the second half with a three-point play that made it 98-95 with two minutes left in the third quarter. Banchero hit his first five shots and finished 10 of 12 from the field. Atlanta erased an double-digit deficit and used a pair of 12-0 runs to take a 72-62 advantage into halftime. The Hawks outscored Orlando 44-29 in the second quarter. Up next Hawks: Play Friday at Charlotte. Magic: Host Minnesota Friday. [SIGN UP: WSB-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ]

item.title: Europa League: Bournemouth vs. Milan – probable line-ups, where to watch on TV
item.description: Europa League: Bournemouth vs. Milan – probable line-ups, where to watch on TV Alphadjo Cisse will start as a false nine for Milan in their away Europa League game against Bournemouth. It kicks off at 21:00 CET [20:00 BST] at the Vitality Stadium. PERTH, AUSTRALIA – AUGUST 05: Alphadjo Cisse of AC Milan passes the ball during the pre-season match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Optus Stadium on August 05, 2026 in Perth, Australia. (Photo by Janelle St Pierre/Getty Images) The Rossoneri must cope without the suspended Filippo Terracciano and the injured Alexis Saelemaekers, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze and Gonçalo Ramos. The latter suffered a calf injury during the final training session on Wednesday, the eve of the game, and, according to several sources, 20-year-old Italian striker Cisse will replace him. Cisse turns 20 today and is currently Milan’s best scorer with five goals in seven appearances across all competitions. He scored a hat-trick in the Rossoneri’s latest Serie A match against RB Salzburg last week. REGGIO NELL’EMILIA, ITALY – OCTOBER 11: Ruben Amorim Head Coach of AC Milan looks on during the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and AC Milan at Mapei Stadium – Citta’ del Tricolore on October 11, 2026 in Reggio nell’Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) Sky Sport and Gazzetta claim that Mario Gila will rest tonight, making room for Fikayo Tomori. Pervis Estupinan is the favourite over Davide Bartesaghi at left-back, while both Adrien Rabiot and Luka Modric are expected to start on the bench, making room for Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Ardon Jashari and Yunus Musah in the Rossoneri’s three-man midfield. Bournemouth vs. Milan – where to watch on TV The match will be broadcast live on TNT Sports 1, TNT Sports Ultimate and HBO Max in the UK and Ireland and on CBS Sports Network, Paramount+, fuboTV, TUDN USA, TUDN.com, the TUDN App, and ViX in the USA. Football Italia will provide live coverage for this match, plus Ajax-Atalanta in the Conference League, and Juventus-Rennes in the Europa League, with the Bianconeri’s match kicking off at 18:45 CET. Bournemouth vs. Milan – probable line-ups Bournemouth (4-2-3-1): Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Cook; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson. Milan (4-4-1-1): Maignan; Tomori, De Winter, Pavlovic, Estupinan; Moreira, Musah, Jashari, Loftus-Cheek; Hutchinson; Cisse.

item.title: ‘It’s done’ – Skip Bayless names the quarterback he’d trade Dak Prescott for
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Dallas Cowboys fan Skip Bayless has had to watch his team endure a tough start to the 2026/27 season. With six games of the campaign gone, the Cowboys are sitting with a 2-4 record, most recently losing to the Green Bay Packers. Amid a difficult 2026/27 so far, quarterback Dak Prescott has come under fire, including being called embarrassing by someone at the AT&T Stadium after a 24-16 home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who were winless prior to that game. Now, Bayless has suggested he would trade Prescott for Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. Skip Bayless says ‘trade me Jayden Daniels for Dak Prescott’ In a clip shared by Gridiron on X/Twitter , Skip said: “If they want to trade me Jayden Daniels for Dak Prescott. It’s done. Straight up, player for player. Let me have him, I’ll take it.” He continued: “He was available all last year when we went 7-9-1. He’s been available this year; we’re 2-4. Give me Jayden Daniels.” The Cowboys are now set to clash with the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7 of the NFL season. The Eagles have also been inconsistent so far this season, sitting with a 2-4 record ahead of their next game on Monday. As a result, a win for Dallas would see them climb above Philadelphia and into second place in the NFC East. item.title: Lyon predicted XI v Hoffenheim: Rémi Himbert brought back in
item.description: Lyon predicted XI v Hoffenheim: Rémi Himbert brought back in Rémi Himbert’s lack of minutes has come as something of a surprise this season. He started in Olympique Lyonnais’ opener in Ligue 1 against Toulouse FC but has not started since. Paulo Fonseca has called from more from the academy product. When Lois Openda sustained an injury, it was just assumed that Himbert would be the benefactor, however, he continued to be omitted by Paulo Fonseca. However, he is set to lead the line for Lyon when they head to face Hoffenheim in the UEFA Europa League this evening. OL are without Mohamed Ouédraogo, Nicolas Tagliafico, Pavel Sulc, and the aforementioned Openda. The likes of Tyler Morton and Corentin Tolisso ahead of the match against Paris Saint-Germain. That game is scheduled to take place on Sunday night, but due to the protests across France, it could be postponed until Monday. Lyon likely line-up v Hoffenheim Dominik Greif; Ruben Kluivert, Moussa Niakhaté, Felix Bacher, Clinton Mata; Mads Bidstrup, Tanner Tessmann, Noah Nartey; Keito Nakamura, Rémi Himbert, Kail Boudache. (L’Éq) GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Ballon d'Or for Harry Kane? 'Could be a special evening'
item.description: Bayern Munich's Harry Kane celebrates scoring his side's second goal during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Bayern Munich and Arsenal at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Ballon d'Or for Harry Kane? 'Could be a special evening'») Sven Hoppe/dpa Another Man of the Match performance on Wednesday has only highlighted Harry Kane's status as favourite to win the prestigious Ballon d'Or award on Monday. The fact that the awards ceremony is in London, where he was born and played for many years at Tottenham Hotspur, would make it even more special for the England captain. "It'd be a massive honour," Kane told TNT Sport, speaking of "a big evening that could be a special one for me. "I've made it clear I don't like to talk about myself, but I know it'd be a massive achievement if it does happen," he said. Kane, 33, had a stunning assist for Alphonso Davies and converted a penalty in Bayern Munich's 2-2 Champions League draw with Arsenal on Wednesday to become Man of the Match. He scored in a 10th match in a row in the elite event, a feat only Cristiano Ronaldo has achieved before when he netted in 11 games. Wednesday's match will play no role in the award as the votes had to be cast a month ago by one journalist from each of the 100 best countries in the FIFA rankings who rate the past season of players. Kane has long made his case. He scored 73 goals for club and country, won a Bundesliga and German Cup double with Bayern, was league top scorer for a third straight year and helped England come third at the World Cup. "He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves. The year he has had has been remarkable," Arsenal and England midfielder Declan Rice said. Bayern's Tom Bischof said that Kane "certainly deserves it. He doesn't just score goals but also provides assists and is always there for the team. The ball to Phonzie (Da vies) was just sensational." Kane, who agreed that it was "one of my best" passes, is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001. Other top contenders are Lamine Yamal, who won LaLiga with Barcelona and the World Cup with Spain; Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappé who is all-time World Cup top scorer and his compatriot Ousmane Dembelé who helped Paris Saint-Germain defend the Champions League title and won the Ballon d'Or last year. "I try not to think about it too much. We've got one more league game to focus (on Sunday in Freiburg) and then hopefully I can enjoy the day and evening on Monday," Kane said.

Kane, 33, had a stunning assist for Alphonso Davies and converted a penalty in Bayern Munich's 2-2 Champions League draw with Arsenal on Wednesday to become Man of the Match. He scored in a 10th match in a row in the elite event, a feat only Cristiano Ronaldo has achieved before when he netted in 11 games. Wednesday's match will play no role in the award as the votes had to be cast a month ago by one journalist from each of the 100 best countries in the FIFA rankings who rate the past season of players. Kane has long made his case. He scored 73 goals for club and country, won a Bundesliga and German Cup double with Bayern, was league top scorer for a third straight year and helped England come third at the World Cup. "He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves. The year he has had has been remarkable," Arsenal and England midfielder Declan Rice said. Bayern's Tom Bischof said that Kane "certainly deserves it. He doesn't just score goals but also provides assists and is always there for the team. The ball to Phonzie (Da vies) was just sensational." Kane, who agreed that it was "one of my best" passes, is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001. Other top contenders are Lamine Yamal, who won LaLiga with Barcelona and the World Cup with Spain; Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappé who is all-time World Cup top scorer and his compatriot Ousmane Dembelé who helped Paris Saint-Germain defend the Champions League title and won the Ballon d'Or last year. "I try not to think about it too much. We've got one more league game to focus (on Sunday in Freiburg) and then hopefully I can enjoy the day and evening on Monday," Kane said.

item.title: Angry Carrick ready 'to deal with what's next' as pressure mounts
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick reacts following the UEFA Champions League match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium. (is associated with: «Angry Carrick ready 'to deal with what's next' as pressure mounts») Luca Rossini/PA Wire/dpa Michael Carrick says he has "got to deal with what's next and see what that looks like" after Manchester United's catastrophic night in Como piled the pressure on the furious manager. The former midfielder last season steered the Red Devils to a third-place finish and Champions League return, having improved the mood, performances and results following Ruben Amorim's rocky reign. But Carrick now appears to be facing the same fate as every other manager since Sir Alex Ferguson after United's winless run extended to a seventh match in Wednesday's 4-1 humbling at Como. The 45-year-old walked over to apologise to the travelling support following a chastening loss that saw skipper Bruno Fernandes publicly question the manager's approach in Italy. Those comments, coupled with an alarming display, raise serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth. "I'm bitterly disappointed," he said. "I'm frustrated, more than frustrated. I'm really angry, to be honest. "But you've got to move on, you've got to deal with what's next and see what that looks like. "At this moment in time, there's a lot to do before that next game, to get the team ready, because that was a difficult night for everyone." In truth, it has been a difficult start to the season for all connected to United. Carrick's side have won just one of their seven Premier League matches and their seven-point haul represents the club's worst return at this stage since 1986. They fell at the first hurdle of the League Cup in embarrassing fashion to Brighton and have lost Champions League games at Atletico Madrid and Como after opening with a win against minnows Sabah. That 4-0 triumph six weeks ago is their last victory in all competitions and there were few signs on the shores of Lake Como that things will improve, especially given under-performing captain Fernandes' comments. Asked if he felt the United squad were still playing for him given those remarks and the group's efforts in Italy, under-fire Carrick said: "It shouldn't be (about) me. "It's not about playing for me, it's about playing for this football club. It's the responsibility that comes (with it). "I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters and giving my best - absolute best - all the time, care about it. My whole life is wrapped around it. "Listen, it might go well, it might not go so well, but I genuinely give everything that I possibly can. "It's really not about me and the relationship. It's about what we all give - players, staff - for this football club." United are yet to confirm when they will preview Sunday's match against Bournemouth, or indeed whether Carrick will be the one facing

item.title: Porsche's IMSA GTP programme set to end: Could Penske switch to Cadillac?
item.description: Motorsport photo Porsche will withdraw its factory operation from the GTP class of the IMSA SportsCar Championship at the end of 2027, according to Motorsport.com's sister title Motorsport-Total.com. This stems from a decision made a year ago. Under the original contract, Penske would have continued running Porsche's 963 LMDh on a factory basis for one more season in both IMSA and the World Endurance Championship before the programme came to an end. However, during negotiations over the winding down of the programme, Porsche decided to terminate its Hypercar effort, including the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans, at the end of 2025. In return, Penske was allowed to compete as Porsche's factory team in the US for one year longer than originally planned. The decision also made sense for the Volkswagen Group brand. In the WEC, Porsche felt it had little chance of competing against the superior Le Mans Hypercars (LMH) with its LMDh prototype, while the US remains a key market for the company. But how does Porsche view the current situation? "We will be competing in IMSA with our factory programme in 2027. We will not comment on any further speculation," a Porsche spokesperson told Motorsport-Total.com when asked about the matter. Will Penske switch to another manufacturer despite its Porsche contract? The most intriguing developments are taking place behind the scenes at Penske. The organisation founded by motorsport legend Roger Penske is exploring the possibility of returning to the WEC - and Le Mans - as early as next year with a privately-entered Cadillac. That would make sense, as few things matter more to 89-year-old Penske than winning the French endurance classic outright. The victory remains missing from the resume of the hugely successful motorsport executive. Currently, Jota runs a pair of Cadillac V-Series.R on a factory basis in the WEC, including at Le Mans. IMSA regular Action Express will also compete at Le Mans with a Cadillac in 2027. Wayne Taylor Racing, however, will not return next year after entering a car in both 2025 and 2026. In theory, that would leave room in the field for a fourth, privately entered Cadillac run by Penske. #7: Porsche Penske Motorsports, Porsche 963, GTP: Roger Penske #7: Porsche Penske Motorsports, Porsche 963, GTP: Roger Penske What speaks against a full WEC season for Penske with Cadillac The question is what consequences such a move would have. Would Penske be allowed to run a privately entered Cadillac in another series alongside its Porsche commitments, or would that violate its contract with Porsche? And could Penske even switch to Cadillac in IMSA as early as 2027? According to information obtained by Motorsport-Total.com, a Penske Cadillac entry at Le Mans in 2027 is highly likely. A full WEC season, however, would probably come too soon, particularly as the team would have to enter two cars, as required under the regulations. Porsche's statement suggests that its IMSA programme will also continue

But how does Porsche view the current situation? "We will be competing in IMSA with our factory programme in 2027. We will not comment on any further speculation," a Porsche spokesperson told Motorsport-Total.com when asked about the matter. Will Penske switch to another manufacturer despite its Porsche contract? The most intriguing developments are taking place behind the scenes at Penske. The organisation founded by motorsport legend Roger Penske is exploring the possibility of returning to the WEC - and Le Mans - as early as next year with a privately-entered Cadillac. That would make sense, as few things matter more to 89-year-old Penske than winning the French endurance classic outright. The victory remains missing from the resume of the hugely successful motorsport executive. Currently, Jota runs a pair of Cadillac V-Series.R on a factory basis in the WEC, including at Le Mans. IMSA regular Action Express will also compete at Le Mans with a Cadillac in 2027. Wayne Taylor Racing, however, will not return next year after entering a car in both 2025 and 2026. In theory, that would leave room in the field for a fourth, privately entered Cadillac run by Penske. #7: Porsche Penske Motorsports, Porsche 963, GTP: Roger Penske #7: Porsche Penske Motorsports, Porsche 963, GTP: Roger Penske What speaks against a full WEC season for Penske with Cadillac The question is what consequences such a move would have. Would Penske be allowed to run a privately entered Cadillac in another series alongside its Porsche commitments, or would that violate its contract with Porsche? And could Penske even switch to Cadillac in IMSA as early as 2027? According to information obtained by Motorsport-Total.com, a Penske Cadillac entry at Le Mans in 2027 is highly likely. A full WEC season, however, would probably come too soon, particularly as the team would have to enter two cars, as required under the regulations. Porsche's statement suggests that its IMSA programme will also continue in 2027. And according to reports, there is no alternative to Penske as the team's factory partner. That does not suggest the US outfit will switch to Cadillac in IMSA before the end of its Porsche commitment. One important point should not be overlooked: Even if Porsche's factory programme ends early, that would not automatically mean the Porsche 963 disappears from IMSA. The prototype, developed by Multimatic, can continue to be raced by privateer teams. JDC-Miller ran a 2025-spec 963 in IMSA this year and won a race at Laguna Seca with Laurin Heinrich and Tijmen van der Helm. Could Porsche return to the WEC with a prototype? A potential prototype comeback by Porsche in the top class of the WEC and at Le Mans in the medium term has not been ruled out. At this year's Le Mans, the organisers provided an early view into what the Hypercar/GTP class could look like in 2030. Rather than balancing the two existing concepts - Le Mans Hypercar (LMH) and LMDh - against each other through Balance of Performance, the series will adopt a common technical rulebook. BoP is still expected to be used to equalise cars built by different manufacturers. Cadillac and Porsche are regarded as driving forces behind these discussions, although that does not necessarily mean either manufacturer will return. "A decision on whether, when and how we will return has not been made, but we are involved in the discussions," Porsche motorsport boss Thomas Laudenbach confirms. "And when you are at the table as a manufacturer discussing technical regulations, you have to look at them from a technical perspective. And that is what we are doing." However, Porsche is not working on a new car at this stage. Read Also: Porsche boss Laudenbach says he is "not happy" with how things were handled by IMSA in 2026 To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Revealed: Why Real Madrid star Arda Guler decided to STEAL Kylian Mbappe's goal during Champions League win against RB Leipzig
item.description: Real Madrid C.F. v RB Leipzig - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid youngster Arda Guler has lifted the lid on his decision to snatch a goal away from teammate Kylian Mbappe during the club's recent European exploits. The Turkish international was in a jovial mood following a dominant display that saw Los Blancos brush aside RB Leipzig at the Bernabeu. A ruthless performance against Leipzig Los Blancos secured a resounding 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig during matchday three of the Champions League. The Spanish giants produced a clinical display, with Guler playing a starring role at the heart of their midfield. The Turkey international was a constant threat, capping off a stellar individual performance by finding the back of the net for his side's second goal of the evening. However, the 21-year-old's strike raised a few eyebrows. Mbappe floated a header towards goal, only for Guler to cheekily nick it right in front of the goalmouth to claim the strike for himself. The goal-line theft did little to stall Madrid's momentum, as Mbappe later added a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side. Record signing Yan Diomande then rounded off the rout to seal a dominant European triumph at the Bernabeu. No apologies to the Frenchman FBL-EUR-C1-REAL MADRID-LEIPZIG Speaking to Real Madrid TV after the final whistle, the midfielder was quick to poke fun at his decision to poach the goal from his illustrious teammate. Guler noted that the French superstar's lethal finishing meant there was no need to worry about him missing out on the action. "I stole the goal from Mbappe, but that’s because I knew he’d score another one. So, no problem," Guler joked during his post-match duties. His lighthearted prediction proved remarkably accurate, as the French superstar did indeed go on to net Real's third goal of the match. Beyond the lighthearted banter, the 19-year-old was eager to highlight the squad's immense work rate across the pitch. "We’re really pleased because I think we played brilliantly, both with and without the ball. I think we put in a great performance and we’re very happy," he added. The Bernabeu factor The convincing victory served as another reminder of the relentless standards demanded in the Spanish capital. For Guler, maintaining that ruthless edge is simply part of the job description when wearing the famous white shirt. "This is what we have to do. We’re Real Madrid, and we have to win every match," the midfielder insisted. He also pointed to the home crowd as a driving force behind their dominant displays, noting: "It’s a key factor because when we play at home, in front of our fans, we try to give it our all for them." With momentum building, Guler fired a clear warning shot ahead of Sunday's massive domestic clash against Barcelona. "It’s a big match, a top-class fixture, and we’ll give it our all to win. We’re ready," he concluded. All eyes on El Clasico imago-sport-1084537410.jpg

item.title: Super Bowl contenders: are the NFL’s unbeaten teams as perfect as they seem?
item.description: Patrick Mahomes greets Chiefs fans after yet another win. Photograph: Jamie Squire/Getty Images San Francisco 49ers (6-0) Who would have thought the 49ers would be here after a rough old offseason? Head coach Kyle Shanahan’s participation in training camp was limited due to a serious car crash , team owner Jed York’s visit to an Ohio trailer park did not end well , and one player after another endured serious injuries. Despite all this, San Francisco are full of positive vibes. They are top of a tough division and their immense defense, led by the intensity of players such as safety Malik Mustapha and Fred Warner, is complemented by an equally impressive offense. Related: Troy Aikman and Joe Buck: what next for the NFL’s $165m TV power couple as they head for a split? Brock Purdy’s record-setting quarterback rating has grabbed the headlines – and rightly so, as his laser accuracy on aggressive downfield throws sets the 49ers offense apart. But there are warnings Purdy’s offensive surge may not last. Pablo Torre pretty much debunked the 49ers’ electrical substation conspiracy theory, but injuries are piling up in the receiving corps. The team have four wide receivers on injured reserve, plus Brandon Aiyuk, who is in self-imposed exile . Purdy had found relief in the form of future Hall of Famer Mike Evans, but the 33-year-old left Monday’s win over the Washington Commanders with achilles pain and is also dealing with fractured ribs. And when Evans is off the field, Purdy struggles. On Monday, Evans caught three passes for 94 yards as the Niners appeared to be cruising at half-time. Without him, the offense went three and out three times, and only just hung on to beat the Commanders. The three-game lead the 49ers have in the NFC West should see them walk into the playoffs. But if Purdy can’t find healthy, reliable targets, the Niners will see another promising campaign end against the big boys in the postseason. Verdict: not quite the real thing Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) The Chiefs are back. After they limped to a 6-11 finish last season, their record is spotless, and the AFC West – thanks in part to the Los Angeles Chargers’ implosion – already looks sewn up. Patrick Mahomes is back from the ACL tear he suffered in 2025, and the offense is no longer solely relying on the quarterback to paper over the cracks: the acquisition of running back Kenneth Walker III looks to be the move of the offseason. item.content:encoded: Patrick Mahomes greets Chiefs fans after yet another win. Photograph: Jamie Squire/Getty Images San Francisco 49ers (6-0) Who would have thought the 49ers would be here after a rough old offseason? Head coach Kyle Shanahan’s participation in training camp was limited due to a serious car crash , team owner Jed York’s visit to an Ohio trailer park did not end well , and one player after another endured serious injuries. Despite all this, San Francisco are full of positive vibes. They are top of a tough division and their immense defense, led by the intensity of players such as safety Malik Mustapha and Fred Warner, is complemented by an equally impressive offense. Related: Troy Aikman and Joe Buck: what next for the NFL’s $165m TV power couple as they head for a split? Brock Purdy’s record-setting quarterback rating has grabbed the headlines – and rightly so, as his laser accuracy on aggressive downfield throws sets the 49ers offense apart. But there are warnings Purdy’s offensive surge may not last. Pablo Torre pretty much debunked the 49ers’ electrical substation conspiracy theory, but injuries are piling up in the receiving corps. The team have four wide receivers on injured reserve, plus Brandon Aiyuk, who is in self-imposed exile . Purdy had found relief in the form of future Hall of Famer Mike Evans, but the 33-year-old left Monday’s win over the Washington Commanders with achilles pain and is also dealing with fractured ribs. And when Evans is off the field, Purdy struggles. On Monday, Evans caught three passes for 94 yards as the Niners appeared to be cruising at half-time. Without him, the offense went three and out three times, and only just hung on to beat the Commanders. The three-game lead the 49ers have in the NFC West should see them walk into the playoffs. But if Purdy can’t find healthy, reliable targets, the Niners will see another promising campaign end against the big boys in the postseason. Verdict: not quite the real thing Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) The Chiefs are back. After they limped to a 6-11 finish last season, their record is spotless, and the AFC West – thanks in part to the Los Angeles Chargers’ implosion – already looks sewn up. Patrick Mahomes is back from the ACL tear he suffered in 2025, and the offense is no longer solely relying on the quarterback to paper over the cracks: the acquisition of running back Kenneth Walker III looks to be the move of the offseason. It was likely that last season’s Super Bowl MVP would be a solid get for a Chiefs rushing attack that averaged a sluggish 4.2 yards per carry last season. But Walker’s production has made the Seattle Seahawks look a little foolish to let him go. Kansas City picked him up for $14.35m a year, making him only the ninth-most expensive running back in the league. Did the Chiefs think Walker would be the NFL’s leading rusher coming into Week 7? Unlikely, especially as the Chiefs have already had their bye week. His 665 rushing yards still top the charts, as do the team’s 5.5 yards per carry . Walker’s penchant for explosive big plays has been the biggest transformation for Kansas City. He already has seven carries of more than 20 yards. The Chiefs managed just three all of last year. The knock on Kansas City is that Walker’s rampage has come amid a soft schedule to start the season. But if he overpowers his former employers – and their formidable defense – on Sunday night the rest of the league should be very worried. Verdict: the real thing Minnesota Vikings (5-0) The Vikings have an important talent when it comes to going the distance: the ability to win ugly. The Seahawks pulled off the same trick last season on the way to winning the Super Bowl. Now Minnesota are doing the same thing with a similarly dominant defense leading the charge. How important is the defense to the Vikings? They are the first team to go 4-0 while not scoring an offensive touchdown in multiple games (wins over Miami and Chicago) since the Detroit Lions in 1934. Perhaps more importantly for the Vikings’ championship hopes: their offense has shown signs of waking up. In their last game, a 23-13 victory over the Saints before the bye week, Kyler Murray had his best day in purple and gold. He looked reliable as the team’s starting quarterback, with an 80% completion rate, 229 passing yards and a highlight-reel touchdown throw that Justin Jefferson caught in triple coverage. As is the case with Evans and the 49ers, Jefferson unlocks a much higher level of production from Murray. The difference for the Vikings is their defense is a cut above the 49ers’ unit. They aren’t one of the best defenses – they are the best. Brian Flores’s blitz-heavy package led by Dallas Turner on the edge and linebacker Blake Cashman has conceded just five touchdowns so far. Verdict: the real thing Buffalo Bills (5-1) OK, the Bills have lost a game, but we’re throwing them in here as they’ve been the best of the rest. You have to admire Josh Allen’s fondness for high drama – and his defense-shredding talent even more. Buffalo lead the league in scoring with four of their five wins coming in box-office shootouts. It’s never dull on the other side of the ball either: Buffalo’s defense has allowed the most yards per game (386.8) of anyone in the league, bar the leaky Lions. The question is whether having such an abject defense is sustainable for the rest of the season. One key metric – stopping teams on third down – suggests they are in for a rough ride against elite opposition in the playoffs. What’s worse is that they started the season poorly in that category and have gotten progressively worse. The NFL average for stops on third down is about 40%. In Week 2, the Lions were successful on third down 36% of the time against the Bills. Last Sunday the Raiders had 58% success in the same scenario. With Allen at the controls, the Bills will always have a shot; it’s just a shame he can’t play both ways. Buffalo need to function at a higher level on defense in fundamental areas to win it all. Verdict: not the real thing Bonus category: the No 1 pick will go to … The Jets have a few shots at “glory”. Their three first-round picks are owned by 2-4 teams: the Colts, Cowboys and the Jets themselves. However, that trio are part of a bunch of franchises with two wins. Many would have been surprised to see the Philadelphia Eagles among those nine teams, but they could sink further. The ongoing saga over Jalen Hurts’s blood clots means the untested Tanner McKee is now the team’s starting quarterback and the Eagles are dealing with a huge injury list. It’s not impossible to imagine they could be in play for the No 1 pick by the end of the season. However, much more likely to be picking first in 2027 are the winless Chargers and Dolphins. Miami are the solid choice to pick first. Their offense has been abysmal, except for one quarter of fluency under zero pressure from the Cincinnati Bengals. Sunday’s matchup will probably highlight the huge gulf in class between the merely bad Jets and the pit of despair that is the Dolphins.

item.title: Ranking the worst trades in MLB history, from Babe Ruth to Pete Crow-Armstrong
item.description: Ranking the worst trades in MLB history, from Babe Ruth to Pete Crow-Armstrong originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Trades come in all shapes in sizes in baseball, from all-in moves, to total tear-downs, to three-team deals and minor upgrades. Some trades are safer than others for general managers, but few truly come without any risk. In a volatile sport that sees stars quickly fade and little-known prospects regularly emerge as valuable pieces, it doesn't take much for a deal to go awry. These trades, however, are the most lopsided in baseball history. Here's a look at MLB's worst trades, from Babe Ruth to Pete Crow-Armstrong. MORE: SN predicts the 2026 World Series 14. item.content:encoded: Ranking the worst trades in MLB history, from Babe Ruth to Pete Crow-Armstrong originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Trades come in all shapes in sizes in baseball, from all-in moves, to total tear-downs, to three-team deals and minor upgrades. Some trades are safer than others for general managers, but few truly come without any risk. In a volatile sport that sees stars quickly fade and little-known prospects regularly emerge as valuable pieces, it doesn't take much for a deal to go awry. These trades, however, are the most lopsided in baseball history. Here's a look at MLB's worst trades, from Babe Ruth to Pete Crow-Armstrong. MORE: SN predicts the 2026 World Series 14. Jose Bautista for Robinzon Diaz, 2008 Blue Jays receive: Jose Bautista Pirates receive: Robinzon Diaz The Pirates can probably get a pass on this one, as Jose Bautista was a 27-year-old utility player on his fourth team when they shipped him to the Blue Jays for a player to be named later — Robinzon Diaz, ultimately — during the 2008 season. Come 2010, Bautista came out of nowhere to hit 54 home runs for the Blue Jays. He would follow it up with an MLB-leading 1.056 OPS in 2011, and Bautista remained one of the AL's best all-around hitters through the 2015 season. While the Blue Jays didn't reach a World Series with Bautista, back-to-back ALCS appearances and an iconic postseason home run in 2015 helped make him a franchise great. Diaz, meanwhile, appeared in 43 games for the Pirates, hitting one home run. It's tough to pin the blame on Pittsburgh, but the Bautista deal turned out to be horribly one-sided. © Pablo Robles-Imagn Images 13. That's well worth what they gave up to get him when he was just 18. The Guardians had only seen 43 professional games from Caminero when they traded him for pitcher Tobias Myers in 2021. Myers, who was 23 at the time, also hadn't made his MLB debut, and it never came in Cleveland. Myers was designated for assignment in July of 2022 after posting a 6.00 ERA across 14 minor-league starts, and the Guardians traded him to the Giants for cash considerations. While Myers broke through with the Brewers in 2024, the Guardians got effectively nothing for a player who is now one of the best young talents in the sport. MORE: Revising Guardians' lopsided trade of Junior Caminero 12. Pedro Martinez for Delino DeShields, 1993 Expos receive: Pedro Martinez Dodgers receive: Delino DeShields The Dodgers knew they had something in Pedro Martinez, but they didn't view him as a starter when he first arrived in the majors. After a solid season as L.A.'s set-up man in 1993, the young Martinez was traded to the Montreal Expos for second baseman Delino DeShields in a deal the Dodgers lived to regret. Martinez would earn the NL Cy Young Award with the Expos in 1997, morphing from a valuable front-of-the-rotation arm into a legitimate ace before being traded to the Red Sox. While Martinez only spent four seasons of his Hall of Fame career in Montreal, the Dodgers only got three uninspiring seasons out of DeShields and would have liked to keep Martinez in their grasp if they could do it all over again. David Banks-Imagn Images 11. Pete Crow-Armstrong for Javier Baez, 2021 Mets receive: Javier Baez, Trevor Williams Cubs receive: Pete Crow-Armstrong The book on Pete Crow-Armstrong's career is largely still unwritten, but the projected NL MVP just turned in what was by some metrics — including fWAR — the most valuable season in the last two decades by anyone not named Aaron Judge. A true five-tool player, Crow-Armstrong tied for the league-lead in home runs while stealing 41 bases and playing spectacular defense in centerfield for the Cubs. "PCA" arrived on the North Side through a 2021 deadline deal that Mets fans will have a hard time forgetting. New York took a chance on Cubs rental Javier Baez but finished only 77-85, with Baez heading to the Tigers in free agency four months later. Crow-Armstrong, meanwhile, has become a superstar for the Cubs and is cost-controlled going forward after Chicago extended him ahead of 2026. Baez played well down the stretch for the Mets in 2021, but his impressive 47 games were not at all worth what Crow-Armstrong has already given the Cubs. MORE: Complete start times, schedule for 2026 World Series 10. Mookie Betts to Dodgers, 2020 Dodgers receive: Mookie Betts, David Price Red Sox receive: Alex Verdugo, Jeter Downs, Connor Wong The Mookie Betts trade still baffles Red Sox fans, who question why a big-market team would ever move on from a homegrown player destined for the Hall of Fame, but the blow might have been easier to take had the franchise made out better in the deal. Originally constructed as a three-team deal with the Twins, the Dodgers split the trade into two separate transactions and sent three players to the Red Sox for Betts and David Price: Alex Verdugo, Jeter Downs and Connor Wong. Verdugo became a useful player for four seasons in Boston, but he wasn't anything more than that due to limited power. Wong actually remains with the Red Sox all these years later as a part-time catcher, while Downs never panned out and appeared in just 14 games for Boston. Betts, meanwhile, won a World Series in his first season with the Dodgers and has since added two more, giving L.A. plenty of value with his versatility even when his bat isn't at its best. Betts has twice finished as the NL MVP runner-up with the Dodgers and has now spent more time in Los Angeles than in Boston as a major-leaguer. MORE: Why the Dodgers' dynasty may be over © Eric Canha-Imagn Images 9. Yordan Alvarez for Josh Fields, 2016 Astros receive: Yordan Alvarez Dodgers receive: Josh Fields The Dodgers have become a machine within the last decade, but there is at least one move they would like to have back. Seeking some bullpen help ahead of the 2016 trade deadline, L.A. acquired reliever Josh Fields from the Astros for a 19-year-old prospect who had signed an international deal barely a month earlier and hadn't yet made his professional debut: outfielder Yordan Alvarez. By 2019, Alvarez was the AL Rookie of the Year despite only playing 87 games. That was only a sign of what was to come, as Alvarez powered the Astros to a World Series win in 2022 and is expected to be named AL MVP in 2026. Fields, meanwhile, posted a 2.79 ERA for the Dodgers down the stretch in 2016 and was a useful relief arm for L.A. over the following two seasons. His 2.0 WAR didn't quite match what Alvarez has given the Astros, though, and it's still jarring to see the Dodgers miss on a player like him. "Looking back on it now, we obviously wish we would have said yes to other names they asked for before him," team president Andrew Friedman later said. MORE: Where Rays, Brewers rank among longest World Series droughts 8. Randy Johnson for Mark Langston, 1989 Mariners receive: Randy Johnson, Gene Harris, Brian Holman Expos receive: Mark Langston, Mike Campbell A young Randy Johnson had only made 10 starts for the Expos when he was traded to the Mariners in a five-player deal early in the 1989 season. Could the future of baseball in Montreal have been different if not for this deal? The same could be said about baseball in Seattle, where Johnson played a central role in the franchise's 1990s surge. Johnson spent parts of 10 seasons with the Mariners, earning five All-Star selections and AL Cy Young honors in 1995. item.title: Romano names three candidates as Julian Nagelsmann is “sounded out” to become next Man United manager
item.description: Romano names three candidates as Julian Nagelsmann is “sounded out” to become next Man United manager Antonio Conte, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe are expected to feature prominently in consideration over the Manchester United job if the club dismiss Michael Carrick , whilst a fourth name is “appreciated” by a United board member. Carrick’s strong start has unravelled rapidly Carrick initially returned as head coach in January, following Ruben Amorim’s departure, and earned a contract until 2028 after guiding United to third place with 11 victories from 16 matches. The situation deteriorated sharply this season. Sunday’s draw at Leeds left United with seven points from seven Premier League fixtures and only one league win. It was followed by last night’s thumping 4-1 Champions League defeat at the hands of Serie A side Como. The situation has changed at United Speaking on his YouTube channel after the defeat , Fabrizio Romano said the situation at United has become untenable. “So this is something not acceptable at all from Manchester United… [t]o lose 4-1 against Como for sure is absolutely humiliating,” he said. “The real change between this game and the other games, it’s also in the players…[it] was Bruno Fernandes to go and speak and saying something about the staff. Is the staff deciding? Then he gave his own opinion, they don’t want to go man-to-man. Then Carrick replying and saying, we went man-to-man in the second half and that’s how we conceded. “That interview was strong because we are talking about Bruno Fernandes. This is not a normal player… this is the player of Manchester United, the face of Manchester United.” “For the very first time we have players at Manchester United not so happy with the current situation. And that’s something that we can consider as a big change compared to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 weeks ago.” Next manager The transfer guru then went on to discuss the likely candidates to replace Michael Carrick if he is sacked. First, he ruled out Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni. “There have been several clubs over the last one or two years asking about Scaloni availability, and the answer was always no, Argentina, no, only Argentina, no, I want to stay with Argentina. And today Lionel Scaloni has decided to put pen to paper and to sign and stay as Argentina coach until the World Cup 2030.” Romano then spoke about Antonio Conte. “Antonio Conte would be ready this year to take a job mid-season, and that’s a big difference to what he always did, almost always in his career, apart from the Tottenham chance. Manchester United have someone on their board who really appreciates Fabian Hürzler, but that’s it at the moment. He’s completely focused on Brighton. Fabregas is completely involved in the Como project. Fabregas is in love with the Como project, and so Fabregas was never gonna leave in summer 2026. He wanted to lead Como into Champions League football.” Final Thoughts Lionel Scaloni and Cesc Fabregas highly unlikely to leave their current roles. Antonio Conte, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe all serious candidates available immediately. Someone on the United board is championing a move for Fabio Hurzeler. item.title: New deal for Harry Kane would represent massive win for Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by Carina Johansen / NTB / AFP via Getty Images) / Norway OUT | NTB/AFP via Getty Images Bayern Munich securing Harry Kane’s future would be about much more than keeping one of the most prolific strikers in world football. It would reaffirm the club’s ability to attract and retain elite talent while ensuring that Vincent Kompany’s attack remains built around one of its most important players. Respected German football journalis t and author Raphael Honigstein, whose work has appeared in The Athl etic and The Guardian , believes Bayern already pulled off a major coup by convincing Kane to leave the Premier League in the first place. Speaking to Casino Guru , he explained why the England captain’s continued happiness in Munich makes a new deal feel like a na tural outcome. “Yeah, of course. I think the big coup is that they’ve managed to get him in the f irst place,” Honigstein said. Honigstein noted that Kane’s move to Bayern was not necessarily viewed as a realistic possibi lity by many outside Munich. The club had laid the groundwork well in advance and took advantage of a summer when Europe’s biggest clubs wer e not all competing for the same kind of striker. Now, Kane appears to have found the right environment to continue developing, both p rofessionally and personally. “I think on the pitch, you can see how he’s becomi ng an even better player, that he’s grown in terms of his all-round game even further,” Honigstein said. Kan e’s influence extends well beyond his goalscoring. His experience, leadership, and ability to link play have made him central to Bayern ’s identity, while playing for a dominant team creates even more opportunities for him to deliver extraordinary numbers. As Honigstein ex plained, playing for a club that regularly controls matches domestically and competes at the highest level in Europe means Kane gets more touches, more cha nces, and more opportunities to score. There is also the personal side of the equation. Munich offers Kane and his young family an attractive lifestyle, with access to the mountains, lakes, skiing, and neighboring countries such as Austria and Italy. Taken together, those factors make his reported willingness to exten d his stay far less surprising. For Bayern, keeping Kane would provide continuity, protect a cornerstone of Kompany’s project, and help maintain the club’s status among Europe’s elite. Finding a striker capable of matching his production would be an enormous chall enge, making a new contract one of the most important pieces of business the club could complete. As Honigstein’s assessment makes clear, B ayern did not simply sign a world-class goalscorer. They found a player who appears to love the club, the city, and the footballing environment around him. Ensuring that relationship continues for years to come would be a significant vic tory for Munich. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Man Utd Forced Into January Transfer U-Turn After Benjamin Sesko Update
item.description: Will Bryan Mbeumo be the centre-forward until January? Manchester United have struggled so far this season after Michael Carrick took the reins on a permanent basis. As the interim head coach, Carrick brilliantly guided the Reds to a third-place finish last term, which seemed nearly impossible when he originally took over. That form earned him the full-time role, but Carrick's side are finding it difficult to consistently perform in the new campaign. Their main issues lie in defence, where the board failed to strengthen in the summer. Left-back and centre-back are both concerns for United, especially with recent injuries. However, United are also struggling in attack, as there is currently no fit senior striker at the club. Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Joshua Zirkzee can all play there, but none are natural number nines. Benjamin Sesko started twice before the international break but has since been out with an injury, and the latest updates regarding the Slovenian are not positive. Sesko suffers setback It was revealed before Manchester United's mid-week clash with Como in the Champions League that Sesko could be out of action for a prolonged period. The Sun states that Sesko ‘suffered a setback’ during his rehabilitation and that there are internal ‘fears’ that he could be out until 2027. The striker is said to have ‘undergone thorough checks’ and 'United are concerned that he faces a spell of up to four months out’, with the club ‘braced’ for him to be out until February at the latest. There will be hopes that Sesko's injury will not be that serious but there is a possibility that United play the majority of the campaign without an actual striker. Carrick will need support from those above him, and a new striker should now be a priority in the January transfer window. Bruno Fernandes Reveals Michael Carrick Decision As Errors Continue Manchester United were well below par against Como in a 4-1 Champions League defeat. Will Man Utd make a January signing? After missing out on signing players for several key positions in the summer, the January window does give Manchester United a chance to solve at least one issue mid-season. However, the Reds are usually not big spenders in the January window. It initially seemed that if any signings were made, it would be to strengthen the defence. The backline at Old Trafford is clearly the biggest weakness, but Sesko's injury could lead to a U-turn in United's transfer strategy as a striker may become the priority. Fans would clearly like the Reds to bolster both their attack and defence in the mid-season window, but it seems like an unlikely prospect, and United will likely choose which is more important for the rest of the season.

item.title: RB Leipzig’s Christoph Baumgartner marks emotional comeback and reunion with Yan Diomande
item.description: RB Leipzig’s Christoph Baumgartner marks emotional comeback and reunion with Yan Diomande Christoph Baumgartner marked his long-awaited return to action for RB Leipzig with an assist in Wednesday evening’s 4-1 Champions League defeat to Real Madrid before offering glowing praise for former teammate Yan Diomande. The Austrian international entered in the 78th minute at the Santiago Bernabéu, making his first competitive appearance in more than four months after a serious tendon injury also cost him the opportunity to represent his country at the 2026 World Cup. Baumgartner required only seven minutes to make an impact. The 27-year-old supplied Tidiam Gomis with an excellent outside-of-the-foot pass for Leipzig’s only goal of the evening. For Baumgartner, however, simply returning to the pitch carried considerably greater significance. “It was a very emotional day for me, in a game like this, against an opponent like this, in a stadium like this – it’s extremely cool,” Baumgartner said after the match. “I’ve been through the most difficult phase of my career, perhaps even of my life. It’s unbelievably fun to be back on the pitch.” The comeback comes after a difficult summer interrupted what had comfortably been Baumgartner’s strongest season since joining Leipzig. The former Hoffenheim midfielder registered 13 goals and ten assists in the Bundesliga last term before suffering the injury that ruled him out of the World Cup and Leipzig’s entire preseason. Baumgartner’s return also represented another significant step in a remarkable turnaround from where his Leipzig career stood little more than a year ago. The Austrian rejected reported interest from Crystal Palace in August 2025 and publicly reiterated his desire to remain at Leipzig before establishing himself as one of the club’s most productive players. Baumgartner delighted to reunite with Diomande Wednesday’s fixture also provided Baumgartner with the opportunity to reunite with former Leipzig teammate Yan Diomande. The Ivorian attacker produced Real Madrid’s fourth goal against his old club, offering another reminder of the ability that made him one of European football’s most coveted young players before leaving Saxony. Baumgartner has never hidden his admiration for the youngster. Baumgartner praised Diomande as a “top talent” following Leipzig’s 6-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last December , highlighting not merely the winger’s attacking ability but also his willingness to make recovery runs and contribute defensively. Four months later, Baumgartner went even further by describing Diomande as an “exceptional player with world class potential” . The reunion thus carried some special significance for Baumgartner. “I love Yan,” Baumgartner told reporters in the mixed zone. “He’s a wonderful guy and an amazing football player. I’m really happy for him that he can now prove how good he is. All of us in the Leipzig locker room know that he’s one of the best talents in the world. All of you

The Austrian rejected reported interest from Crystal Palace in August 2025 and publicly reiterated his desire to remain at Leipzig before establishing himself as one of the club’s most productive players. Baumgartner delighted to reunite with Diomande Wednesday’s fixture also provided Baumgartner with the opportunity to reunite with former Leipzig teammate Yan Diomande. The Ivorian attacker produced Real Madrid’s fourth goal against his old club, offering another reminder of the ability that made him one of European football’s most coveted young players before leaving Saxony. Baumgartner has never hidden his admiration for the youngster. Baumgartner praised Diomande as a “top talent” following Leipzig’s 6-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last December , highlighting not merely the winger’s attacking ability but also his willingness to make recovery runs and contribute defensively. Four months later, Baumgartner went even further by describing Diomande as an “exceptional player with world class potential” . The reunion thus carried some special significance for Baumgartner. “I love Yan,” Baumgartner told reporters in the mixed zone. “He’s a wonderful guy and an amazing football player. I’m really happy for him that he can now prove how good he is. All of us in the Leipzig locker room know that he’s one of the best talents in the world. All of you guys in Madrid will have a lot of fun with him.” “He’s a great player,” Baumgartner continued. “When he gets more confidence and gets more time on the pitch with the other big players, he will show that he’s incredibly good. Also a nice goal from him today. I hope he will score a lot in the future. I wish him all the best.” GGFN | Peter Weis

item.title: Jarell Quansah tight-lipped about future amid Liverpool, Arsenal and Real Madrid interest
item.description: Jarell Quansah tight-lipped about future amid Liverpool, Arsenal and Real Madrid interest Speaking ahead of Bayer Leverkusen’s UEFA Europa League clash against OFI Crete on Thursday, Jarell Quansah dodged questions about his future, amid interest from Liverpool, Arsenal and Real Madrid. “I just have to concentrate on playing this season,” he explained. “I’m playing as many games as possible and trying to improve – I can’t do more than that.” According to Sky Germany , Liverpool hold a reported €70m buy-back clause for the Englishman, which will become active in 2027 after the €70m option expired. However, the Reds also face competition from Arsenal, who have been without William Saliba this season due to a back injury – which has kept him out since the end of France’s World Cup campaign – and Real Madrid. Holding a market value of €50m, per Transfermarkt , Quansah has featured in eight of Leverkusen’s nine games across all competitions this season, starting five of them. GGFN | Daniel Pinder

item.title: Monaco predicted XI v Freiburg: Paris Brunner to start, Folarin Balogun ineligible
item.description: Monaco predicted XI v Freiburg: Paris Brunner to start, Folarin Balogun ineligible Paris Brunner, who missed the weekend’s defeat to FC Lorient due to suspension, is set to start for AS Monaco against SC Freiburg in the UEFA Europa Conference League on Thursday night. The competition in the forward line is slightly weakened on European nights, with USMNT forward Folarin Balogun not eligible to play, having been left out of the squad. The former Arsenal forward is not the only absentee. Eric Dier and Stanis Idumbo are both out with injuries. Both may be out until the international break, however, for Dier at least, there is hope that he could return before then. One of the biggest question marks for Monaco revolves around who will start on the right of the attack. Matthis Abline is in contention, as are Edan Diop and Mamadou Coulibaly. Monaco likely line-up v Freiburg Lukas Hradecky; Christian Mawissa, Mohammed Salisu, Sadibou Sané, Jordan Teze; Lamine Camara, Edan Diop; Mathys Detourbet, Aleksandr Golovin, Mamadou Coulibaly; Paris Brunner. (L’Éq) GFFN | Luke Entwistle
