item.title: New Zealand vs. India live score, win probability, chances of victory for 1st T20I in Christchurch
item.description: New Zealand host India in the opening T20I of a five-match series at Hagley Oval on Thursday, October 22. It is the start of a 12-match tour that runs through to December 1. There is an obvious edge to the fixture. The last time these sides met, India beat New Zealand by 96 runs in the T20 World Cup final in March, and Mitchell Santner's team will not have forgotten how comprehensively that night went against them. MAKE YOUR BET WITH DAFABET AND GET UP TO 200% WELCOME BONUS India are without Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya, while New Zealand have lost Rachin Ravindra to a dislocated shoulder along with Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes, which has thinned out both attacks before a ball has been bowled. Conditions could be the decisive factor at a ground India have never played a men's T20I on. The evening is forecast to stay dry but cold, with temperatures dropping towards 14°C by the closing overs. Live scorecard New Zealand vs. India 1st T20I: Live updates and toss result New Zealand batting updates After 15 overs, New Zealand are 158/3 The Black Caps maintain a blistering scoring rate of 10.53, navigating through India's middle overs to reach 158/3 at the end of the 15th. Despite Arshdeep Singh making a breakthrough to send back Daryl Mitchell for 28, India's bowlers have struggled to contain the boundary flow. Glenn Phillips capitalised on sloppy fielding and full tosses, smashing Axar Patel for three boundaries in the 14th over to bring the spinner's spell to a painful close. Debutant Bevon Jacobs showed no big-stage nerves, dispatching Arshdeep for a towering six on debut to keep the hosts firmly on target for a daunting 200-plus total in Christchurch. After 10 overs, New Zealand are 98/2 India's bowling unit effectively clawed their way back into the contest during the middle-over phase in Christchurch. With Finn Allen threatening to take total control of the innings after his 24-ball 45, Axar Patel struck the decisive blow, inducing a false shot that was safely taken at deep long-off. The tandem of Axar Patel and Nitish Kumar Reddy expertly checked the run rate, preventing further boundary damage and dropping the current run rate under 9.50. With Glenn Phillips (10*) joining Daryl Mitchell (15*) at the crease, the Black Caps hold crucial wickets in hand to construct a massive finish over the remaining ten overs. After 6 overs, New Zealand are 65/1 New Zealand made full use of the Powerplay, putting India's bowling attack under relentless pressure from the start. Tim Seifert and Finn Allen took on Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Arshdeep Singh, boundaries flowing freely despite some early lateral movement. Mayank Yadav provided India's sole breakthrough in the fifth over, using his express pace to get Seifert (24) caught behind by Sanju Samson. However, the momentum stayed with the hosts as Allen (33*) and Mitchell (7*) closed out the sixth over with a 16-run assault against Axar Patel. Toss result India won the toss and chose to field first. New Zealand

item.title: Bayern Munich confirm new investor in major ownership shake-up
item.description: Bayern Munich confirm new investor in major ownership shake-up Bayern Munich have confirmed that the Viessmann Generations Group will become the club's fourth external shareholder in a behind-the-scenes shakeup. Der Rekordmeister have announced that the investment group, headed by Max Viessmann, will acquire a stake of just under 6.7 per cent in FC Bayern München AG, while the parent association FC Bayern München e.V's stake is reduced from 75 to 70 per cent. Existing external shareholders, Adidas, Audi and Allianz will also see their holdings diluted, with each company owning approximately 8.33 per cent up to this point. Back in August, Münchner Merkur reported that Bayern were considering selling a five per cent stake for approximately €250 million, but the precise financial terms of the newly announced agreement have not yet been confirmed. Max Viessmann will also join the club's supervisory board, with the 37-year-old's arrival expanding the group from nine to ten. The German businessman, who already serves on the administrative advisory board, heads the Viessmann family's investment group. The family built its fortune through the heating and climate technology industry before selling Viessmann Climate Solutions to US company Carrier Global in 2023. Viessmann's involvement with Bayern is not entirely new, with the club maintaining a commercial partnership with Viessmann Climate Solutions since 2018, and the agreement was extended until 2029 earlier this year. Speaking about the agreement, Bayern president Herbert Hainer emphasised the financial benefits of bringing another long-term partner on board, “The Viessmann Generations Group stands for values such as tradition, ambition and innovation, just like FC Bayern," Hainer said. “We are delighted to have a long-standing partner at our side whom we have known for many years - and who further strengthens our group of shareholders with a family-owned international company that takes a long-term, generational view.” Hainer also highlighted the additional financial flexibility the investment will provide. “This step strengthens the ownership structure of FC Bayern München AG. In addition, a significantly improved equity base gives us greater room for manoeuvre at a time of constant change.”

item.title: 6 NBA teams make history for all the wrong reasons in their season openers
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images 6 NBA teams make history for all the wrong reasons in their season openers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Opening night in the NBA always brings optimism, fresh jersey designs, and the promise of a championship chase. However, for six franchises, the new season started in historically embarrassing fashion. For the first time in NBA history, six different teams lost their season openers by 20 or more points on the exact same slate. Leading the dubious charge were the Chicago Bulls, who suffered a soul-crushing 135-92 loss to the Toronto Raptors . Toronto held Chicago to a dismal 32% shooting from the field, while Chicago’s fourth overall pick turned in an ugly minus-45 rating on the night to leave the Bulls with a 43-point deficit. Not far behind were the Phoenix Suns, who dropped their opener 124-84 against the Portland Trail Blazers. Portland dominated every facet of the game, handing Phoenix a brutal 41-point beatdown to start their campaign. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The blowout epidemic did not stop there. Superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 35 points in his debut for the Miami Heat, but it was not enough to prevent a 131-106 defeat at the hands of Anthony Edwards and the Minnesota Timberwolves . Minnesota shot lights out to cruise to a 25-point victory, while the Sacramento Kings also dropped their opener by 25 points after a painful second-half collapse. Out West, Luka Dončić and the Los Angeles Lakers steamrolled the Golden State Warriors in a 127-105 victory. Dončić stuffed the box score with 28 points, eight rebounds, and seven assists in just 30 minutes, leaving Golden State on the wrong end of a 22-point margin despite some early trash talk from Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. Rounding out the record-setting evening, the Utah Jazz fell 123-103 to the Memphis Grizzlies, sealing a 20-point loss to cap off the night. While an 82-game regular season offers plenty of time for redemption, these six teams now share an unwanted spot in the league record books. Opening night provided a swift reality check across the basketball world. item.title: Luka Doncic Reveals Why He Cursed Out Yaxel Lendeborg
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 21: Yaxel Lendeborg #1 and Gui Santos #15 of the Golden State Warriors defend against the dribble of Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers during the first half of a game at Crypto.com Arena on October 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty The Los Angeles Lakers scored a dominant opening night victory that featured Luka Doncic talking all night long. Multiple viral moments saw Doncic cursing out Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg in the first half. The Lakers clearly won the battle on and off court with Luka declaring he was getting in Lendeborg when the rookie got called for a technical foul. View this post on Instagram Following the 127-105 victory, Doncic was asked by Malika Andrews about what caused him to throw some insults towards Lendeborg: “I think everybody knows when somebody starts talking, you get a different me. item.title: Leipzig manager backs Real Madrid to win La Liga and Champions League after 4-1 defeat: ‘Their quality is hard to match’
item.description: Leipzig manager backs Real Madrid to win La Liga and Champions League after 4-1 defeat: ‘Their quality is hard to match’ RB Leipzig manager Marin Demichelis believes Real Madrid have the quality to compete for both La Liga and the Champions League after his side suffered a 4-1 defeat against Jose Mourinho’s team . Despite feeling Leipzig had performed well enough to avoid trailing at half-time, the Argentine acknowledged that Madrid’s individual brilliance proved decisive, while singling out Arda Guler and Yan Diomande for their influence on the contest. Demichelis explains why Real Madrid are difficult to stop Leipzig were competitive during the opening stages, but Real Madrid’s ability to turn promising situations into decisive moments ultimately separated the teams. Demichelis pointed to the Spanish side’s attacking quality as the biggest obstacle his players faced, arguing that even a strong performance can end in defeat against opponents capable of producing something extraordinary. “The same thing often happens here. You play a great match and then Madrid end up beating you. They have the ability to push forward with players who can turn a game on its head. “That’s why we pressed them high up the pitch. We bunched up near our own goal and felt comfortable there. After that, Real Madrid’s individual quality is hard to match. “Some of the goals came about that way. Real Madrid will undoubtedly be one of the favourites to win La Liga and the Champions League,” he said. Leipzig manager questions half-time scoreline Demichelis says Real Madrid favourites to win the UCL. (Photo by Fabio Deinert/Getty Images) Although Demichelis acknowledged Real Madrid’s superiority after the break, he was unhappy with the final result and felt Leipzig had not received a fair reflection of their first-half performance. Bernardo Silva’s goal on the stroke of half-time gave Madrid the advantage, leaving the visitors with a difficult task after the interval. “I’m not very happy because we’ve lost again and conceded four goals. Personally, I’d say my team played well with the ball. “Unfortunately, Madrid showed their class and their ability. My personal opinion is that we didn’t deserve to go into half-time a goal down. “After that, Real Madrid controlled the game better in the second half,” he explained. Demichelis praises Arda Guler and Yan Diomande Demichelis also highlighted two players who contributed to Real Madrid’s victory. Demichelis has praised Arda Guler. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) Arda Guler’s performance came as little surprise to the Leipzig manager, who recalled facing a similar tactical setup involving the Turkish international during his time at Mallorca. “I wasn’t surprised by Arda. He has the ability to make all sorts of things happen. “When I was at Mallorca, we came up against a similar line-up, with Arda cutting in from the wing, and it didn’t surprise us,” he recalled. item.title: PSG face UEFA punishment after Barcelona complain over controversial banner
item.description: PSG face UEFA punishment after Barcelona complain over controversial banner Paris Saint-Germain are facing potential disciplinary action from UEFA after Barcelona complained about an inflammatory banner displayed by PSG supporters before their 4-2 Champions League victory at the Parc des Princes. According to Mundo Deportivo , the incident is expected to lead to a financial penalty, while a partial stadium closure or a warning over future sanctions could also be considered. Barcelona report PSG over chainsaw banner The banner, unveiled before kick-off, featured an image of hands wielding a chainsaw to destroy the Barcelona crest alongside the words “Parisian Massacre”. Other banners displayed during the match reportedly contained the offensive phrase “Puta Barça”. Barcelona confirmed that it would report the incident to UEFA , objecting to imagery the club considered incompatible with the values of respect and fair play expected in football. The complaint places PSG under scrutiny over the conduct of the fans at one of European football’s most prominent club fixtures. As per the outlet, the incident could bring both a financial penalty and additional stadium-related sanctions. However, the final punishment has not been officially confirmed by UEFA. So what happens now? UEFA’s Disciplinary Code prohibits the use of sporting events for non-sporting demonstrations or conduct that discredits football and the governing body. Its regulations also place responsibility on host clubs and national associations for maintaining order and security around matches. The rules state, “Host clubs and national associations are responsible for order and security both inside and around the stadium before, during and after matches. “All associations and clubs must comply with the obligations set out in the UEFA Security Regulations.” The regulations further specify, “They are responsible for any type of incident and may be subject to disciplinary measures and guidelines, unless they can demonstrate that they have not been negligent in the organization of the match.” UEFA also identifies “the use of gestures, words, objects or any other means to convey a provocative message that is not appropriate for a sporting event, in particular provocative messages of a political, ideological, religious or offensive nature” as sanctionable conduct. These provisions give UEFA a basis to examine the display and determine whether PSG should face disciplinary measures. The governing body will now assess the incident before any final punishment can be established.

Carreras, Vinicius and Bernardo returned to the XI while Arda started on the right side with Fede Valverde. The team played some brilliant football at times and looked to attack the opposition throughout the game. There were times it looked like Camavinga was the only midfielder with almost everyone else ahead of him. The players moved around so freely with Arda moving in from the right to pick up th ball in midfield while Bernardo occupied the CF role and Fede made runs down the flank. The transition heavy game and verticality is exactly what Mourinho likes but the freedom the players had is something new from Mourinho and suggests that he’s got a good understanding of the types of players he has in his squad. Vinicius In Free Fall Vinicius had yet another chance to regain his form and build some confidence but looks closer to a player contemplating retirement than one who just got given everything he’s asked for. Vinicius was backed by his teammates all through dips in form and even getting Xabi Alonso sacked. He was given a new contract after protracted negotiations with the club. The new manager has given him a platform to shine and consistently defended him. He plays in his preferred position at his preferred club. But he looks like that’s the last place he wants to be as soon as the game starts. Diomande has replaced him and while Mourinho will not freeze out the Brazilian, the obvious choice for LW isn’t really a matter up for debate. Huijsen On the Ball Dean has his confidence back and while his development on the defensive side of the game will require more patience, he’s been very good this season on both sides of the ball. He’s the kind of player we’re going to enjoy for 10 years. A fantastic signing reminding us why we were so excited to have him in the first place. The transition heavy game and verticality is exactly what Mourinho likes but the freedom the players had is something new from Mourinho and suggests that he’s got a good understanding of the types of players he has in his squad. The new manager has given him a platform to shine and consistently defended him. He plays in his preferred position at his preferred club. But he looks like that’s the last place he wants to be as soon as the game starts. Diomande has replaced him and while Mourinho will not freeze out the Brazilian, the obvious choice for LW isn’t really a matter up for debate. Huijsen On the Ball Dean has his confidence back and while his development on the defensive side of the game will require more patience, he’s been very good this season on both sides of the ball. He’s the kind of player we’re going to enjoy for 10 years. A fantastic signing reminding us why we were so excited to have him in the first place. His ball progression takes a lot of the weight of the midfielders and instantly elevates our possession game while his reading of the game in defence continues to improve as he’s operating on a really high level. Fede at Home on the Right Fede is a complete player. He can do everything. I wouldn’t be surprised if he’s the player lined up to replace Courtois long-term. The Real Madrid captain looks phenomenal on that right side. One cannot begrudge Mourinho for wanting to keep Fede at right back forever. He gives the team so much on both sides of the ball. Our ball progression goes up to another level when Fede is on the right. Barring injuries or suspensions, there’s no tactical reason for Fede to return to midfield this season. Unfortunately, this means Trent has yet another obstacle in his way. Perhaps Mourinho will surprise us with the Trent-Valverde combo for El Clasico.. We live in hope. Arda Güler.. Mágico Arda was born to play this game. He looks so natural. What a talent. Mourinho has given his stamp of approval and the youngster hasn’t looked back. While many of us would agree that RW isn’t the best use of his time, Arda has consistently given his best efforts whenever Mourinho has given him a job. If Arda carries on with his current trajectory, he’s going to be the Toni Kroos replacement everyone’s been harping on about. A Shoutout to Camavinga The Frenchman has been more down than up for a long time now but Mourinho has found a way to inject that confidence and belief into his veins. Camavinga looked more like himself against Leipzig and was showered with praise by Mourinho after the game. He still has some way to go to compete for a regular starting spot but he’s definitely on the right track. One game a time. Mourinho has already shown with Diomande replacing Vinicius that he will reward good performances as long as your rival is not Kylian Mbappe and in all fairness, that ought to be easy to excuse.

item.title: Erik ten Hag recalls being ‘embarrassed’ by Man United after promise broken over keeping player
item.description: Erik ten Hag has revealed he felt “very embarrassed and disappointed” after Manchester United failed to keep a promise not to sell a key player during his time at the club. The Dutchman, who was sacked in October 2024, also backed current head coach Michael Carrick to remain in post in a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic . Now technical director of FC Twente , his boyhood team, Ten Hag appeared to have no hard feelings about his time at Old Trafford , telling the outlet he had “such wonderful memories”. But he was critical of the leadership since Jim Ratcliffe ’s takeover in late 2023, with the Ineos era failing to bring the club back to its glory days. He said: “The takeover process brought a lot of noise, uncertainty with the people, and disruptions. It was difficult to work, that’s clear. It was very complicated.” The Dutchman nearly lost his job shortly before the FA Cup final the following summer but the 2-1 victory over Manchester City gave him a lifeline, with a one-year extension in his contract triggered two weeks after. He said that during crisis talks before the extension was agreed, “They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.” “That’s why I got disappointed. In Ibiza [during talks], we agreed. I said, ‘No selling Scott McTominay ’. We would go aligned in the transfer window. I make an argument, a reason: we don’t have scoring abilities. Scott brings scoring abilities and great mentality. He has United in all his veins. So when they bring up the subject, ‘No’. And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed.” McTominay was sold to Napoli that summer for £25.7m and has flourished there, rapidly establishing himself as a key figure in the squad which won the Serie A title in his first year at the club. United bought Manuel Ugarte with the proceeds from the Scot’s sale. Scott McTominay has become a key figure at Napoli (Getty) Ten Hag also said there were issues regarding the exact nature of his role, foreshadowing Ruben Amorim ’s explosive outburst over being the manager of United rather than the head coach, despite head coach being his formal title. Ten Hag said: “After the first meeting (at Carrington), [Ratcliffe] started talking about the structure in the football club, how the manager should be head coach. I said, ‘OK, let’s discuss, but my contract is different’. I never heard anything. “I always want to cooperate in a club — you can’t do this on your own. You need to find a strategy about philosophy, game model, about team profile, individual profiles. That is what I was used to, but with them there was no communication.” He said dismissing the under-pressure Carrick after a dismal start to the season was “100% not the solution” and put more of the onus on the wider leadership at the club, saying: “The leadership, you need their competence, you need the right strategy. item.title: UFC 333: Volkanovski vs Evloev start time, undercard and how to watch fights this weekend
item.description: This weekend, Alexander Volkanovski and Petr Yan defend their titles in a major double-header at UFC 333 . In the main event in Abu Dhabi, Volkanovski puts his featherweight belt on the line against Movsar Evloev , who will bring an unbeaten record and tricky grappling style against the Australian icon. At 38 years old, the well-rounded Volkanovski will hope not to have lost a step , as the slightest drop-off could cost him against a fighter known for close decisions . Alexander Volkanovski during his second win over Diego Lopes (Getty) In the co-main event, Yan fights Merab Dvalishvili for the third time, having avenged a loss to the Georgian by outpointing him with a masterful showing in December. The bantamweight belt is up for grabs in that fight, just as it was in their second meeting, and a Yan victory could set up a great night for Russia if Evloev follows suit. When is UFC 333? UFC 333 will take place on Saturday 24 October at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. The early prelims will begin at 3pm BST (7am PT / 9am CT / 10am ET), followed by the regular prelims at 5pm BST (9am PT / 11am CT / 12pm ET), then the main card at 7pm BST (11am PT / 1pm CT / 2pm ET). How can I watch it? In the UK , the card will air live on TNT Sports and is also accessible via HBO Max, EE TV, Virgin Media, Amazon Prime Video, and Sky Sports. In the US , Paramount+ will stream the action, with CBS showing a segment of the card. Odds Volkanovski – 10/11; Evloev – 10/11 Yan – 8/15; Dvalishvili – 6/4 Via Betway . item.title: Kompany gives injury update on Bayern duo after Arsenal draw
item.description: Kompany gives injury update on Bayern duo after Arsenal draw Bayern Munich were dealt a double injury blow on Wednesday night, as Min-jae Kim and Luis Díaz both had to come off in their 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League. Kim was substituted at half-time, while Díaz, who had been carrying a knock into the game, was brought on in the second half before being forced off again shortly before full-time. After the game, Bayern head coach Vincent Kompany provided an update on both players, playing down concerns over any serious injuries. “I hope the recovery timelines are similar for both. That means not too long, perhaps less than a week,” he said. “I think we can already rule out any serious injuries.” Both players look likely to miss at least Sunday's Bundesliga away fixture against Freiburg.

item.title: 🔮 The 4️⃣ emerging options for the Manchester United job
item.description: 🔮 The 4️⃣ emerging options for the Manchester United job It's already a crisis! After the crushing 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League, the Manchester United hot seat is under intense scrutiny. With an apparent rift with some senior players and results falling well short of expectations, here are the four main scenarios taking shape for the United managerial job: 1. The emergency option: appoint Eddie Howe quickly Available since leaving Newcastle, Eddie Howe is widely seen in England as the leading contender. He has extensive Premier League experience, favours high-intensity football and is reportedly particularly enthusiastic about the prospect of getting the team back on track straight away. 2. The board's choice: Julian Nagelsmann This is reportedly the option that excites INEOS most. Available since his spell in charge of Germany ended, Nagelsmann would bring tactical discipline, a modern playing philosophy and the iron fist needed to restore order in the dressing room. 3. The experienced option: Antonio Conte Antonio Conte is also named by the English press among the candidates being considered. The Italian specialises in turning teams around and instilling a winning mentality from day one. 4. One last chance for Michael Carrick Despite the speculation and internal tensions with senior players, the board could give Carrick one final reprieve to turn things around in the very next league match against Bournemouth. Another defeat, however, would almost certainly seal his departure. Which do you think is the best option? Let us know in the comments! item.title: Desmond Bane pinpoints where Magic got ‘killed’ by Hawks
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images Desmond Bane pinpoints where Magic got ‘killed’ by Hawks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Orlando Magic fell short against the Atlanta Hawks, 132-125 , in their season opener at Kia Center on Wednesday, spoiling the debut of coach Sean Sweeney. The Magic were outplayed in crunch time, giving up back-to-back three-pointers to Nickeil Alexander-Walker in the last two minutes. Orlando lost to Atlanta for the sixth straight time. After the game, Desmond Bane acknowledged that they shot themselves in the foot, as reported by Sentinel Sports’ Jason Beede. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I don’t think the offense was really the problem. We turned the ball over a little bit too much. They killed us on the rebounds. (They) got a lot of offensive rebounds and got to the free-throw line a lot. Those are two things that we’ve talked about since day one. So those are things that we can definitely clean up,” said Bane. He had 18 points, five rebounds, and three assists. He struggled from the field, shooting 5-of-15, including 3-of-10 from long distance. The Hawks only had two more rebounds than the Magic. They also had three fewer free throws. Orlando gave up 24 points off 21 turnovers. Paolo Banchero led the Magic with 35 points, seven rebounds, and 10 assists. Franz Wagner added 22 points, six rebounds, and five assists, while Wendell Carter Jr. tallied 22 points and seven rebounds. The Magic are trying to establish a new identity in Sweeney’s first year. They have qualified for the playoffs for the last three seasons, but they have not made it past the first round. Bane, Banchero, Wagner, Carter, Jalen Suggs, Anthony Black, and Nikola Vucevic will be tasked with carrying the team. Orlando will host the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday. item.title: The most embarrassing Champions League defeats for English clubs after Manchester United’s Como collapse
item.description: The most embarrassing Champions League defeats for English clubs after Manchester United’s Como collapse Manchester United suffered a European embarrassment at Como in the Champions League this week. The Italian outfit ran out 4-1 winners at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, as the dominant debutants piled more pressure on Michael Carrick's men. Following a humbling result, we've looked at some of the most embarrassing Champions League defeats suffered by Premier League sides. Spartak Moscow 4-1 Arsenal - 2000/01 season Arsenal often struggled when making the trip to Eastern Europe in their first Champions League campaigns. The 2000/01 season saw Arsenal battered twice during trips to the region, losing to Shakhtar Donestk in the first group stage, before opening the second group stage with a big defeat in Moscow. The Gunners opened the scoring inside two minutes, but struggled in the freezing conditions. Marcao's double turned the game around, before further goals from Yegor Titov and Luis Robson saw Spartak stun the Premier League side. Maccabi Haifa 3-0 Manchester United - 2002/03 season Maccabi Haifa secured the most impressive result in their history after humbling a second-string Manchester United side in 2002/03. Sir Alex Ferguson opted to rotate his team with group stage progress assured, though the side still featured big names in Gary Neville, Rio Ferdinand, Paul Scholes, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Diego Forlan. Played in Cyprus due to UEFA's ban on matches in Israel, Maccabi stunned their visitors. Yaniv Katan and Raimondas Zutautas each scored fine goals before future Premier League favourite Yakubu sealed success from the spot. It took Maccabi another 20 years to record their next Champions League win. Arsenal 1-5 Bayern Munich - 2016/17 season Arsenal's gradual decline during Arsene Wenger's latter years reached a nadir during a home humiliation by Bayern Munich in 2017. The Gunners had been beaten 5-1 in Germany during the first leg, and an attempt to restore a semblance of respectability did not go as planned. Arsenal did lead through Theo Walcott, but Laurent Kosielny's red card played its part in a collapse. The Germans were ruthless to run out 10-2 winners on aggregate, the heaviest two-legged Champions League defeat that a Premier League side has ever suffered. Tottenham Hotspur 2-7 Bayern Munich - 2019/20 season Bayern Munich have made a habit of inflicting painful defeats on English opponents, particularly those who reside in North London. The German champions ran riot at Tottenham Hotspur during the 2019/20 season, scoring seven times against the previous season's Champions League runners-up. Ex-Arsenal man Serge Gnabry haunted his former rivals with four goals, as a shellshocked Spurs capitulated under the lights. Bayern went on to be crowned European champions, with this an ominous early warning to their challengers. The feeling was much, much different in the return. The Magpies went toe-to-toe during a five-goal first half that ended with Barcelona one goal ahead, but the second-half saw the Spaniards storm through. Four unanswered goals saw Eddie Howe's side hit for seven.

item.title: Seahawks Get Important Zach Charbonnet Injury Update Before Chiefs Game
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - DECEMBER 28: Zach Charbonnet #26 of the Seattle Seahawks carries the ball for yardage during the game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 03: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers hands the ball off to Zach Charbonnet #26 during the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during a game at Raymond James Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks received one of their most encouraging injury updates of the season on Wednesday, October 21. Running back Zach Charbonnet was listed as a full participant on Seattle’s first injury report ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs, marking another significant step in his recovery from a torn ACL. Charbonnet has yet to play this season after suffering the injury during Seattle’s postseason victory over the San Francisco 49ers in January. His return now appears closer than ever, with the Seahawks preparing for a Sunday Night Football showdown against undefeated Kansas City. But before Charbonnet can make his season debut, Seattle must make an important roster decision. Getty SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA – JANUARY 03: Zach Charbonnet #26 celebrates with Cooper Kupp #10 of the Seattle Seahawks after scoring a touchdown against the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter of a game at Levi’s Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Zach Charbonnet Injury Update Comes Before Critical Seahawks Deadline The Seahawks opened Charbonnet’s 21-day practice window on October 1, allowing him to resume football activities while remaining on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. That window reaches its conclusion on Thursday, October 22, meaning Seattle must activate Charbonnet to its 53-man roster or leave him on the PUP list for the remainder of the season. Wednesday’s full-participation designation is particularly encouraging because Charbonnet had previously been limited as the Seahawks gradually increased his workload. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 03: Zach Charbonnet #26 celebrates with Cooper Kupp #10 of the Seattle Seahawks after scoring a touchdown against the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 03: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers hands the ball off to Zach Charbonnet #26 during the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during a game at Raymond James Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks received one of their most encouraging injury updates of the season on Wednesday, October 21. Running back Zach Charbonnet was listed as a full participant on Seattle’s first injury report ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs, marking another significant step in his recovery from a torn ACL. Charbonnet has yet to play this season after suffering the injury during Seattle’s postseason victory over the San Francisco 49ers in January. His return now appears closer than ever, with the Seahawks preparing for a Sunday Night Football showdown against undefeated Kansas City. But before Charbonnet can make his season debut, Seattle must make an important roster decision. Getty SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA – JANUARY 03: Zach Charbonnet #26 celebrates with Cooper Kupp #10 of the Seattle Seahawks after scoring a touchdown against the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter of a game at Levi’s Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Zach Charbonnet Injury Update Comes Before Critical Seahawks Deadline The Seahawks opened Charbonnet’s 21-day practice window on October 1, allowing him to resume football activities while remaining on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. That window reaches its conclusion on Thursday, October 22, meaning Seattle must activate Charbonnet to its 53-man roster or leave him on the PUP list for the remainder of the season. Wednesday’s full-participation designation is particularly encouraging because Charbonnet had previously been limited as the Seahawks gradually increased his workload. Head coach Mike Macdonald had already indicated that the running back might return against Kansas City. “Zach is going to have a full week’s worth of reps, so that’s exciting, and there’s a possibility that you could see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that’s exciting,” Macdonald said during his October 19 press conference, according to the team’s official website. The latest injury report strengthens the case for Charbonnet’s availability, although full participation does not guarantee that he will play Sunday. Getty SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA – JANUARY 03: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers hands the ball off to Zach Charbonnet #26 during the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during a game at Raymond James Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Seahawks Could Get Much-Needed Help at Running Back Against Chiefs Charbonnet’s potential return comes at an important time for Seattle’s rushing attack. Rookie running back Jadarian Price remains on injured reserve after suffering a chest injury, leaving the Seahawks to rely heavily on Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. Charbonnet would bring a proven scoring threat to that rotation. During the 2025 regular season, the former UCLA standout recorded 730 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns on 184 carries across 16 games. He has scored 20 rushing touchdowns over his last two regular seasons. Those numbers help explain why Seattle could benefit from having him available near the goal line, especially as the offense searches for more consistency. However, Macdonald’s suggestion that Charbonnet might play “in some capacity” leaves open the possibility of a managed workload in his first game back from a significant knee injury. The Seahawks also received a potentially encouraging development along the offensive line, with starting right guard Anthony Bradford returning to practice this week. Bradford was listed as limited Wednesday while working toward his own return from injured reserve. Is Zach Charbonnet Playing Against the Chiefs? Charbonnet has not officially been cleared to make his 2026 season debut against the Kansas City Chiefs, but Wednesday’s full-participation designation is a positive sign. The Seahawks must first activate him from the PUP list, and his availability for Sunday’s game will depend on the team’s decision and his continued progress. Seattle hosts Kansas City on Sunday, October 25, on Sunday Night Football. For a Seahawks offense missing one of its young running backs and preparing to face an undefeated opponent, getting Charbonnet back would provide a timely reinforcement. Wednesday’s injury report brought him another step closer. The next development should be considerably more definitive: a roster move. item.title: Shola Ameobi: ‘I thought: how can I be most useful to Newcastle? Then the cog started turning’
item.description: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey “There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says. “There were situations where I had to sprint to get away from groups of lads who didn’t like me because of what I looked like.” Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were, he says, “lots of moments” like that. “It was almost as if I had to hide myself to be able to do what I love to do. It wasn’t a very nice feeling, having to worry about getting from A to B. It was just part of my world. I had to be more aware of my surroundings and what I was doing.” Continue reading...

item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. Continue reading...

The manager was delighted with the fight that his players showed, Declan Rice earning a deserved point with an 82nd-minute equaliser. Arsenal had led through Eberechi Eze, who came on in the 10th minute for the stricken Saka, before Harry Kane took centre stage. The Bayern striker set up Alphonso Davies for 1-1 before giving his team the lead from the penalty spot. Continue reading...

item.title: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
item.description: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own. Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged. Continue reading...

item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
item.description: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Champions League drama galore – so why do we feel hollow?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. I broke out in a cold sweat reading about how they ‘give power to the players’. The stuff of nightmares, really” – Rowan Sweeney. Roberto De Zerbi wants Spurs to be a family ( yesterday’s Football Daily )? And he thinks playing for or with a family will avoid relegation? Well, I have this uncle. He’s called Weird Uncle Fiver (now there’s a throwback – Football Daily Ed), and he loves to [snip – Football Daily lawyers, and time-travelling pedants]” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
item.description: Teenager produced man-of-the-match performance against Villarreal and has learned from Salah, says Reds captain The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.description: Wiegman says she ‘cannot think of a better job in football’ She can target three European titles in row with Lionesses Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract to continue as the head coach of England women for Euro 2029. Her deal was due to expire after the World Cup next summer and this extension gives her the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row. Wiegman, who took on the role in September 2021 , also led her native Netherlands side to European Championship glory in 2017 and has reached the final of the past five major tournaments, twice finishing as a World Cup runner-up. item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Michael Butler
item.content:encoded: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...

item.description: Get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week, featuring the insights of experts such as Ada Hegerberg and Magdalena Eriksson Join us as we delve deeper into the wonderful world of women’s football in our weekly newsletter. It is informative, entertaining, global, critical – when needed – and, above all, passionate. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more.
